result.markdown: --- title: "[Graph.get_degree_distribution()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method}" body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 toc-depth: 3 page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Get degree distribution as a mapping from degree to count. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L13575-L13612){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python Graph.get_degree_distribution() ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} ![Degree distribution](/assets/graphs/algo-degree-distribution.light.svg){.lightbox fig-alt="A small bar chart showing the degree distribution P(k) of a graph. Bars correspond to degrees 1 through 5 along the x-axis, with heights giving the number of nodes at each degree. The modal degree (k=3, the tallest bar) is highlighted in the accent color; the other bars are drawn in a muted ink." width="100%"} Returns a histogram of node degrees, showing how many nodes have each degree value. Useful for analyzing network topology and identifying hub nodes or scale-free properties. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [dict[int, int]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Dictionary mapping degree values to the number of nodes with that degree. ::: ## Examples {.doc-examples} Four spokes each have degree `1`, while the hub alone has degree `4`: ::: {#15db471c .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec graph = ( ec.Graph() .add_node(label="Hub") .add_node(label="A") .add_node(label="B") .add_node(label="C") .add_node(label="D") .add_edge("Hub", "A") .add_edge("Hub", "B") .add_edge("Hub", "C") .add_edge("Hub", "D") ) graph.get_degree_distribution() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` {1: 4, 4: 1} ``` ::: :::
